# meshstack_workspace_user_group (Resource)

A group of users in a meshStack workspace. Bind the group to a workspace or project role with `meshstack_workspace_group_binding` or `meshstack_project_group_binding`.

~> **Members:** Set `spec.members` to manage the group's complete member list from this resource. Leave it unset to manage the members elsewhere, for example with `meshstack_workspace_user_group_member` or in meshPanel. Do not combine `spec.members` with `meshstack_workspace_user_group_member` resources for the same group: each would remove the members the other adds.

~> **Deletion:** Deleting the group also deletes all of its role bindings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "meshstack_workspace_user_group" "example" {
  metadata = {
    name               = "my-user-group"
    owned_by_workspace = data.meshstack_workspace.example.metadata.name
  }
  spec = {
    display_name = "My User Group"

    # Usernames, not email addresses. Omit members to manage them elsewhere,
    # for example with meshstack_workspace_user_group_member.
    members = [data.meshstack_user.example.metadata.name]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `metadata` (Attributes) Identifiers of the workspace user group. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--metadata))
- `spec` (Attributes) Configuration of the workspace user group. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--spec))

### Read-Only

- `status` (Attributes) Information meshStack keeps about the group. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--status))

<a id="nestedatt--metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metadata`

Required:

- `name` (String) Identifier of the workspace user group. A group binding names the group by it in `subject.name`.
- `owned_by_workspace` (String) Identifier of the workspace that owns the group.


<a id="nestedatt--spec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec`

Required:

- `display_name` (String) Name of the group as meshPanel shows it.

Optional:

- `egid` (String) Identifier of the group in the system it comes from, such as the group's ID in your identity provider. meshStack keeps it unique across all workspace user groups.
- `members` (Set of String) Usernames of the group's members. Each one must belong to an existing meshUser; look it up with the `meshstack_user` or `meshstack_users` data source. When you set this attribute, Terraform removes every member it does not list. When you leave it unset, Terraform leaves the members as they are.
- `tags` (Map of List of String) Tags of `meshWorkspaceUserGroup`. Only the tags you declare here are managed by Terraform.


<a id="nestedatt--status"></a>
### Nested Schema for `status`

Read-Only:

- `disabled_usernames` (Set of String) Members whose user is disabled, for example by SCIM. A disabled user stays a member and regains access when the user is enabled again.
- `source_system` (String) System that manages the group, such as `SCIM` for a group your identity provider synchronizes. Null for a group created with Terraform.

## Import

Use the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) with an appropriate `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  # full group identifier <workspace-identifier>.<group-identifier>
  id = "my-workspace.my-user-group"
  to = meshstack_workspace_user_group.example
}
```

To generate the full resource configuration from the existing remote state, add the `import` block above to your configuration and then run:

```shell
tofu plan -generate-config-out=generated_resources.tf
# Terraform equivalent:
terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated_resources.tf
```

Copy the generated configuration into your root module to start managing the resource with OpenTofu or Terraform.
Note that the generated configuration may require minor adjustments or cleanup, so always run `tofu plan` / `terraform plan` afterwards to verify 
that the configuration fully matches the imported state and that no unintended changes are pending.
If the plan only shows the import of the resource (no other changes), you can run `tofu apply` / `terraform apply` to complete the import. From that point on,
the resource is fully managed via OpenTofu or Terraform.
